reviewScope: Ten frozen physical sites ranked from the network-backed suspicious queue. A suspicious severity is treated as a distance flag, then checked against the named waterbody, public access identity, access geometry, route role, and imagery. This record preserves completed decisions while the remaining frozen sites continue through review.

sites.name: Arrowhead Mountain Lake public boat ramp, Fairfax
sites.reason: The endpoint is at the public Arrowhead Mountain Lake ramp. Vermont Fish & Wildlife identifies the access area, satellite imagery shows the lake-side ramp, and Vermont DEC identifies the lake at the downstream end of the Lamoille mainstem. The large flowline distance was a waterbody-model mismatch, not evidence that the launch was misplaced.

sources.finding: Vermont Fish & Wildlife's public access-area source supports the named Arrowhead Mountain Lake access.
Vermont DEC describes the Lamoille River mainstem reach as ending at Clarks Falls Dam at the downstream end of Arrowhead Mountain Lake.

sites.publicationAction: retain-coordinate-and-route; map terminal lake connection in audit control

sites.name: Pearl Rock Canoe/Kayak Launch
sites.coordinateMethod: Chickasaw County confirms the named canoe launch on the Cedar River. The guide-published pin was about 600 feet west on 305th Street. The replacement uses the named Google Maps launch-place coordinate, checked against current aerial imagery showing the public access drive at the river-side landing.
sites.reason: The original guide coordinate resolves to the road rather than the mapped launch. The replacement matches the named access marker and shoreline evidence.

sources.finding: Chickasaw County identifies Pearl Rock Canoe Launch Site and its Cedar River access.
The Cedar River paddling guide publishes the previous coordinate and route context; its location is displaced from the named launch on imagery.
Named launch-place record supplies the replacement coordinate; aerial imagery was manually checked on 2026-09-18. This is imagery-derived, not surveyed agency GPS.

sites.validation: Both affected route audits have zero suspicious endpoints and no source issues. Pearl Rock now resolves to the exact named water-entry control; the remaining 191-foot flowline offset is review-only and reflects generalized hydrography.
sites.publicationAction: keep-both-public-routes; regenerate route geometry and registry

sites.name: Princeton Jefferson Street / Hiestand Park Landing
sites.reason: The prior point 43.8512,-89.1289 is over 600 feet from the matched Fox River flowline. The City of Princeton identifies the kayak launch and boat pier at Hiestand Park; the Princeton Visitors Guide places the public launch off Mechanic Street. Current aerial imagery shows the river-entry pier on the east bank. The replacement coordinate 43.852380,-89.133973 marks its visible water-entry end with 50-foot uncertainty; it is imagery-derived, not surveyed.

sources.finding: City page documents the 2018 kayak launch and boat pier at Hiestand Park.
Princeton Visitors Guide locates the public launch off Highways 23/73 on Mechanic Street and describes an accessible kayak/canoe EZ Launch.
Current aerial imagery shows the park pier extending from the Fox River's east bank; map coordinate checked at the visible water-entry end, not surveyed.

sites.validation: The public-route audit checked 2 endpoints, found zero suspicious results and zero source issues; Hiestand matches the named water-entry control. The all-inventory audit of the second route also cleared Hiestand, but that route remains withheld for a separate 1,275-foot Old St. Marie access-point failure.

sites.name: Schram Park public boat ramp
sites.coordinateMethod: The City of Manchester confirms a boat ramp at Schram Park for Maquoketa River access; the Iowa DNR water-trail guide marks the park as an alternate put-in. The old point was in Manchester's residential street grid. The replacement uses the river-side Schram Park place marker checked against aerial imagery on 2026-09-18.
sites.reason: The old coordinate was about 2,416 feet from the park access and did not identify the boat ramp. The replacement is at the documented public ramp area.

sources.finding: City of Manchester confirms a boat ramp at Schram Park for Maquoketa River access.
Iowa DNR identifies Schram Park as an alternate put-in on the Maquoketa water trail.
Named park marker and satellite imagery place the public access at the river side of the park. Coordinate is imagery-derived, not a surveyed city point.

sites.validation: Targeted route audit: 5 endpoints checked, zero suspicious, zero source issues; the Schram access point matches the named water-entry control. The remaining 331-foot flowline offset is review-only, with NHD water proximity within 100 feet.
sites.publicationAction: keep-route-public; regenerate route geometry and registry

sites.name: Baileysville WVDNR public access
sites.reason: An older state fishing guide publishes the stored point, but that listing does not establish a boat entry. The current WVDNR GIS layer has an active CR 14 Bridge carry-down/pull-off about 0.8 mile east. Aerial review of the saved point does not establish a public boat carry or landing. Do not silently substitute CR 14 for the named Baileysville water-trail endpoint.

sources.finding: The older guide publishes 37°35′21″ N, 81°40′45″ W as Baileysville - Guyandotte River, but does not describe boat access there.
Current WVDNR fishing/boating layer identifies active CR 14 Bridge, Guyandotte River, Carry Down, Pull-Off at 37.5876617,-81.6645737.
Current District 4 guide lists CR 14 Bridge as a river access and the Guyandotte Campground downstream; it does not resolve the stored point as the paddling endpoint.

sites.reopen: Confirm the intended public Baileysville put-in/take-out with a current WVDNR water-trail map or access inventory and georeference its legal carry and water entry. Use CR 14 only if the water-trail itinerary confirms it is the intended site.

sites.name: Canton Bridge Access / Canton County Park
sites.reason: Jackson County names Canton Bridge Access at County Road E17. Iowa DNR's water-trail material documents the Canton-to-Royertown corridor. The broad Maquoketa route name had failed the control's exact South Fork name match; an explicit source-backed connected-water-trail relationship now makes the control visible to the audit. The coordinate remains a bridge/park anchor, not a surveyed river-entry point.

sources.finding: Jackson County names Canton Bridge Access at the E17 bridge.
Iowa DNR documents the connected Maquoketa/North Fork water-trail corridor and guided Canton-to-Royertown paddle.

sites.validation: Targeted audit now reports review with the authoritative access-anchor source instead of suspicious; the 609-foot flowline offset remains a human review item.

sites.name: Neal Bridge Take-Out
sites.reason: The Bureau of Reclamation confirms Neal Bridge as the downstream take-out, and Idaho Fish and Game identifies the reach from Neal Bridge / Forest Road 189 upstream. The stored RiverFacts point (43.55194,-115.73723) is about 3,900 feet west of the mapped bridge and reverse-geocodes to Blacks Creek Road. No reviewed source georeferences the required river-left landing immediately before the bridge, so the stored point is rejected and the expert route is withheld rather than silently moved to the bridge axis.

sources.finding: Bureau of Reclamation identifies the Danskin-to-Neal Bridge take-out above Arrowrock backwater; it does not publish exact landing coordinates.
Idaho Fish and Game identifies the canyon run from Danskin Bridge to Neal Bridge and describes extremely limited access.
Idaho Fish and Game locates the regulated South Fork reach from Neal Bridge (Forest Road 189) upstream to Anderson Ranch Dam.
The USGS monitoring station is named for Neal Bridge and places the river station near 43.55056,-115.72194.
OpenStreetMap maps the Neal Bridge crossing at 43.5502113,-115.7218012; this locates the bridge axis, not the exact public landing.
The community source underlying the stored endpoint publishes 43.55194,-115.73723, which is substantially west of Neal Bridge.

sites.reopen: Locate and verify the legal river-left landing just upstream of Neal Bridge from a current Forest Service/Reclamation map or direct managing-agency confirmation; replace the held route endpoint only when that water-entry point is supported.

sites.name: Copper Creek Boat Access, NPS Road 213
sites.reason: The old coordinate is about 650 feet from the matched Skagit flowline. NPS identifies the public Copper Creek take-out; the county's approved permit decision places it south of SR 20 east of MP 111.5 and describes a 40-foot gravel boat ramp at the water's edge. Current aerial imagery shows the ramp/landing at the end of the access road. The replacement 48.591100,-121.373204 is imagery-derived with 75-foot uncertainty, not surveyed.

sources.finding: NPS names the Copper Creek Take-Out near SR 20 milepost 112 as a public Skagit access.
The approved permit decision locates the facility south of SR 20 immediately east of MP 111.5, confirms public river access, and documents a 40-foot gravel ramp at the water's edge.
Current aerial imagery was checked at the access road end; the selected coordinate is an imagery-derived ramp-edge location, not a surveyed coordinate.

sites.validation: Targeted audits checked all 6 endpoints across the three affected routes, found zero suspicious results and zero source issues. The corrected Copper Creek endpoints match the named authoritative ramp control; all are within 100 feet of NHD waterbody geometry. Route-scoped geometry regeneration is pending full refresh.

sites.name: Wes Block Trail Access
sites.reason: The previous point was 482 feet from mapped water. The Jane Addams Trail operator verifies Wes Block Trail Access at 2636 W Fairview Road with parking and a boat launch; Illinois Paddling Council documents a kayak launch completed in 2022. Current imagery checks the named trailhead marker at 42.3300675,-89.6663288 as the public access area. Keep the coordinate explicitly as a 75-foot-uncertainty parking/carry anchor because the reviewed sources do not georeference the 2022 launch's exact water-entry edge.

sources.finding: Jane Addams Trail lists Wes Block Trail Access at 2636 W Fairview Road with parking and boat-launch amenities.
Illinois Paddling Council documents completion of a new kayak launch at Wes Block Landing in August 2022.
Aerial imagery checks the named Wes Block trailhead/public access area; it does not resolve the precise launch-edge coordinate.

sites.validation: Targeted audit checked 2 endpoints, found zero suspicious results and zero source issues. Wes Block matches the named authoritative access-area control; the endpoint is 361 feet from the NHD flowline, so retain the exact-water-entry caveat for field review.

sites.name: Millertown Bridge Access / Monmouth corridor
sites.reason: The stored point is about 29,850 feet southeast of the public access and reverse-geocodes to 116th Avenue. Jackson County places Millertown Bridge Access at the 30th Avenue bridge; OSM bridge geometry and current aerial imagery locate the crossing at 42.124508,-90.857821. The coordinate is an access/bridge-axis anchor with 100-foot uncertainty, not a surveyed wet-edge landing.

sources.finding: Jackson County names Millertown Bridge Access at the 30th Avenue bridge, three miles north of Monmouth.
Iowa DNR water-trail map labels Millertown in the Maquoketa corridor.
30th Avenue bridge geometry (bridge=yes) places the crossing at 42.124508,-90.857821; this is the road axis, not the exact water-entry point.
The rejected stored point reverse-geocodes to 116th Avenue, far southeast of Millertown.
Current aerial imagery shows the access road and crossing at the Maquoketa; used to check the bridge-axis access anchor, not to claim a surveyed wet-edge coordinate.

sites.validation: Targeted audit checked 3 endpoints, found zero suspicious results and zero source issues; the Millertown put-in is a named authoritative access anchor and 33 feet from its control. Route-scoped geometry was regenerated.
